title: Structural Insights into the Activation of Human Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor by the Environmental Contaminant Benzo[a]pyrene and Structurally Related Compounds.
authors: Kwong, Hok-Sau; Paloni, Matteo; Grandvuillemin, Loic; Sirounian, Savannah; Ancelin, Aurelie; Lai-Kee-Him, Josephine; Grimaldi, Marina; Carivenc, Coralie; Lancey, Claudia; Ragan, Timothy J; Hesketh, Emma L; Balaguer, Patrick; Barducci, Alessandro; Gruszczyk, Jakub; Bourguet, William
one_liner_zh: 该文通过冷冻电镜解析人AHR转录因子与配体苯并芘的复合物结构并结合分子对接研究配体结合机制，虽聚焦配体而非DNA互作，但AHR为TF且结构建模方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a ligand-dependent transcription factor belonging to the bHLH/PAS protein family and responding to hundreds of natural and chemical substances. It is primarily involved in the defense against chemical insults and bacterial infections or in the adaptive immune response, but also in the development of pathological conditions ranging from inflammatory to neoplastic disorders. Despite its prominent roles in many (patho)physiological processes, the lack of high-resolution structural data has precluded for thirty years an in-depth understanding of the structural mechanisms underlying ligand-binding specificity, promiscuity and activation of AHR. We recently reported a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of human AHR bound to the natural ligand indirubin, the chaperone Hsp90 and the co-chaperone XAP2 that provided the first experimental visualization of its ligand-binding PAS-B domain. Here, we report a 2.75 A resolution structure of the AHR complex bound to the environmental pollutant benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P). The structure substantiates the existence of a bipartite PAS-B ligand-binding pocket with a geometrically constrained primary binding site controlling ligand binding specificity and affinity, and a secondary binding site contributing to the binding promiscuity of AHR. We also report a docking study of B[a]P congeners that validates the B[a]P-bound PAS-B structure as a suitable model for accurate computational ligand binding assessment. Finally, comparison of our agonist-bound complex with the recently reported structures of mouse and fruit fly AHR PAS-B in different activation states suggests a ligand-induced loop conformational change potentially involved in the regulation of AHR function.
abstract_zh: 芳香烃受体（AHR）是一种配体依赖性转录因子，属于bHLH/PAS蛋白家族，能响应数百种天然及化学物质。它主要参与抵御化学损伤和细菌感染或适应性免疫反应，同时也涉及从炎症性疾病到肿瘤性疾病等病理状态的发展。尽管AHR在许多（病理）生理过程中扮演重要角色，但三十年来，缺乏高分辨率结构数据阻碍了对其配体结合特异性、混杂性及激活机制的结构学深入理解。我们近期报道了人源AHR与天然配体靛玉红、伴侣蛋白Hsp90及共伴侣蛋白XAP2结合的冷冻电子显微镜（cryo-EM）结构，首次实验可视化了其配体结合PAS-B结构域。在此，我们报道了AHR复合物与环境污染物苯并[a]芘（B[a]P）结合的2.75 Å分辨率结构。该结构证实了PAS-B配体结合口袋存在双位点特征，其中几何约束的主结合位点控制配体结合特异性和亲和力，而次级结合位点则有助于AHR的配体结合混杂性。我们还报道了一项B[a]P同系物的对接研究，验证了B[a]P结合的PAS-B结构可作为精确计算配体结合评估的合适模型。最后，将我们的激动剂结合复合物与近期报道的小鼠和果蝇AHR PAS-B在不同激活状态下的结构进行比较，提示存在一种配体诱导的环构象变化，可能参与AHR功能的调控。
